correctness.rationale: Every finite-state positive-flushing system has a unique bounded stationary solution. Conditional moment balance yields the exact resolvent; detailed balance gives a symmetric positive-semidefinite conjugate with rank n−1. Its derivative is a signed combination of at most n−1 reciprocal-square kernels. A self-contained Rolle induction proves that such a nonzero combination has at most n−2 distinct positive zeros. The explicit strictly increasing three-state flow and load example has a Cramer-verified rational mean, exactly one positive derivative root, a true global maximum, and exact endpoint limits. checker.py verifies polynomial coefficients, derivative and 38 rational stationary balance systems. No finite test stands in for the general proof.

value.rationale: The count bound converts the number of reversible stochastic discharge regimes into a universal limit on the complexity of the stationary concentration response as environmental persistence changes. It distinguishes the two-regime monotonic case from a three-regime counterexample even with monotonically increasing pollutant loading and flow, where the concentration maximum exceeds the slower-switching endpoint by more than 16 percent. This is a nontrivial structural limitation and a useful theoretical benchmark for testing simplified flow-state models, not merely re-computation of a known matrix inverse. It is conditional, stylized, and not a calibrated environmental risk claim.
